summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for persistent right groin and thigh pain following placement of a new tunneled femoral dialysis catheter. She had recently completed treatment for MRSA bacteremia from a prior catheter. Evaluation revealed no signs of infection, clot, or catheter dysfunction. Ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis, and blood cultures were negative. The pain was attributed to likely scar tissue formation. Her subtherapeutic INR of 0.9 was noted, and warfarin management was recommended for follow-up. She remained on IV vancomycin for completion of her antibiotic course. Headache resolved spontaneously. She was discharged to extended care with pain management, continued antibiotics, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
problems: Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
